title: Week 17 Mastery Quiz · Comparative Political Systems Synthesis

questions.question: Which definition best matches “comparative method”?
options: Protection granted by a state to a qualifying person seeking refuge.
A written international agreement governed by international law.
Systematic comparison used to describe, classify, explain, or evaluate cases.
Money owed by a national government.
questions.explanation: Comparative method means systematic comparison used to describe, classify, explain, or evaluate cases.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “case selection”?
options: The reasoned choice of cases appropriate to a research question.
Cross-border organization of production stages for a good or service.
Failure to investigate or impose accountability for serious violations.
Inability to credibly promise future compliance when power or incentives may change.
questions.explanation: Case selection means the reasoned choice of cases appropriate to a research question.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “most-similar design”?
options: Severe climate impacts that cannot be fully avoided through mitigation or adaptation.
A relationship in which economic structures constrain autonomous development.
Comparison of similar cases with different outcomes.
Use of computational systems to inform or make public decisions.
questions.explanation: Most-similar design means comparison of similar cases with different outcomes.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “most-different design”?
options: Identification of actors responsible for a digital operation.
Comparison of different cases sharing an outcome or relationship.
A difficult-to-exclude resource vulnerable to overuse.
Structured evaluation of preparedness, response, outcomes, and lessons.
questions.explanation: Most-different design means comparison of different cases sharing an outcome or relationship.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “typology”?
options: A record explaining changes made in response to evidence and feedback.
A classification system based on multiple dimensions.
A norm such as humanity, neutrality, impartiality, or independence guiding relief.
Discouraging action by credibly threatening unacceptable costs.
questions.explanation: Typology means a classification system based on multiple dimensions.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “causal inference”?
options: Logical connection among question, method, evidence, findings, and conclusion.
Systematic collection and analysis of health data for action.
A systematic review of required work, evidence, records, and corrections.
Reasoning about whether and how one factor contributes to an outcome.
questions.explanation: Causal inference means reasoning about whether and how one factor contributes to an outcome.

questions.question: Which statement is most consistent with the Week 17 analysis?
options: Comparison requires common concepts and attention to case-specific context.
A single vivid example proves a universal conclusion without qualification.
The most confident source should be accepted without examining authority or method.
Political labels have exactly the same meaning in every country and period.
questions.explanation: Comparison requires common concepts and attention to case-specific context.

questions.question: Which statement is most consistent with the Week 17 analysis?
options: Selecting only convenient cases creates biased conclusions.
The most confident source should be accepted without examining authority or method.
A single vivid example proves a universal conclusion without qualification.
Political labels have exactly the same meaning in every country and period.
questions.explanation: Selecting only convenient cases creates biased conclusions.

questions.question: Which research practice is most appropriate for Comparative Political Systems Synthesis?
options: Trace claims to Country portfolios from Weeks 13–16 and cross-national governance datasets, evaluate authority and context, corroborate material facts, and state limitations.
Choose only evidence that supports the preferred conclusion.
Replace documentary evidence with political identity or intuition.
Use the first search result and treat its summary as conclusive.
questions.explanation: Trace claims to Country portfolios from Weeks 13–16 and cross-national governance datasets, evaluate authority and context, corroborate material facts, and state limitations.

questions.question: Which response most clearly demonstrates senior-level mastery?
options: Use a slogan as the conclusion and omit uncertainties.
Treat legal, causal, and moral claims as interchangeable.
List facts without connecting them to a claim.
Define the terms, compare evidence, explain reasoning, address a serious alternative, and name a revision condition.
questions.explanation: Define the terms, compare evidence, explain reasoning, address a serious alternative, and name a revision condition.

shortResponse: Which concepts best explain similarities and differences across political systems without erasing history and context?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
